Answer: A
Reason: The lateral chest X-ray (Figure 2) demonstrates a well-circumscribed, rounded opacity in the middle mediastinum that causes anterior bowing (displacement) of the trachea. This specific location and mass effect are classic radiographic features of a bronchogenic cyst, whereas lymphomas typically present with more diffuse widening and thymic lesions are located anteriorly without this specific tracheal deviation pattern.
